rationale: Targeted re-check of the four blocking findings from code-review-final.json against the fix-up diff (9a099bc..d19e6c9, 8 files, +167/-17). All four are resolved, each with a test that was observed failing first. No full lens fan-out was re-run. One suspicion was examined on the fix-up diff itself — the new focus-management effect in FileList could in principle steal focus on an unrelated re-render — and was refuted by reading the code: pendingFocusIndex is only ever set inside a row's onRemove handler and is cleared by the effect that consumes it, so no other render path can trigger a focus() call. CR-003 is resolved for every case where a row remains; the empty-list case is explicitly out of reach and recorded as a follow-up (the drop area contains no focusable element at all — its file input is display:none and the dropzone is a plain div without tabIndex, so adding files is currently mouse-only).

finding_status.evidence: src/components/form/FilesDropzone/components/FileListItem.tsx — focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-[rgb(var(--colors-border-accent))]. Test 'gives the remove button a visible focus indicator' asserts the classes and was observed failing first. IMPORTANT correction to the first attempt: the fix originally copied the repo's house style (focus:outline-none + focus-visible:ring-2 + ring colour) and that version was verified in a real browser to render NOTHING — the computed ring resolved to three fully transparent box-shadow layers while focus:outline-none had suppressed the UA outline, so the control ended up with a *less* visible focus state than before the fix. Probing the live page showed ring colours do not resolve anywhere in this project: even a core ring-red-500 computes transparent, because the Tailwind palette is replaced by CSS-variable design tokens and --tw-ring-color is never set. The shipped version therefore styles the outline instead, bound directly to the theme token, and was confirmed in the browser: after Tab the computed style is 'outline: auto 2px rgb(0, 122, 255)', matching --colors-border-accent, and the ring is clearly visible in the After screenshot.

aria-hidden="true" added to BasketSvg (src/components/File.tsx) and CrossSvg (src/pages/skills/components/SkillBundleFilesSection.tsx). Both are covered by tests that failed first. Note the icon mocks in File.test.tsx were changed to forward props — without that the assertion would have passed vacuously against a prop-swallowing stub, exactly the trap the edge-case lens flagged. Scope held to the two delete controls named in the finding; the chevron/preview icons in File.tsx are different controls and were left alone.

src/components/form/FilesDropzone/components/FileList.tsx now records the removed row's index and, after the re-render, focuses the delete button at that index (clamped to the last remaining row, which yields the previous row when the tail was removed). Two tests, both observed failing first: 'moves focus to the next remaining delete button after a row is removed' and 'falls back to the previous row when the last row is removed'. Known limit, recorded as a follow-up rather than silently dropped: when the final row is removed the list unmounts and there is no focusable fallback in the drop area, so focus returns to <body>.

Resolved per the user's decision (distinguish sections): FileListItem takes a fileKind prop ('uploaded' | 'selected', default 'selected') and renders aria-label={`Delete ${fileKind} file ${fileName}`}; FileList passes it explicitly for each section. Test 'distinguishes an uploaded row from a selected row that share a file name' asserts two distinct accessible names for two files literally named spec.pdf, and was observed failing first. Residual, accepted with the decision: two files with the same name inside the same section still share a name — but their removal is then equivalent, so the dangerous asymmetry the finding described is gone.
